character_facts: Honorata is physically vulnerable enough to need a risky operation or mental intervention.
Aghnar still loves both his mother and Oda despite choosing between them.
Aghnar explicitly rejects becoming or continuing as 'Metabarons.'
The robotic attendant addresses Honorata as 'mistress,' indicating subordinate service.
continuity_links: This page centers an unresolved conflict between dynastic continuation of the Castakas and rejection of the warrior code.
Honorata's survival appears contingent on a dangerous procedure, setting up consequences for later pages.
Aghnar's declaration against the Metabarons marks a major turning point in family tradition.
dialogue_meaning: Honorata frames the procedure as one requiring total concentration and solitude.
The machine-assisted intervention is dangerous and leaves her extremely weakened for years.
Aghnar is emotionally torn between loyalty to his mother and commitment to Oda.
Honorata forces a binary choice to determine Aghnar's future allegiance.
Aghnar chooses his wife and also declares an ideological break from the warrior destiny of the Metabarons.
Honorata still interprets his choice as preserving the Castakas bloodline.
locations: A high-tech medical or mental-probe chamber
A partitioned viewing or conversation area adjoining the chamber
lore_facts: Honorata can undergo or direct an advanced mental procedure involving a 'deep-reaching' probe and extreme concentration.
The procedure is so taxing that it would nearly extinguish her energy and require several years of strict isolation afterward.
If that required solitude is broken, Honorata says she will die.
Tonto is present as an assistant or operator during the procedure.
The Castakas line is treated as something that 'must live on.'
Aghnar and Oda have agreed on a future in which the Castakas continue 'but not as warriors.'
The title or role of 'Metabarons' is associated here with a warrior identity that Aghnar rejects.
plot_events: Honorata prepares for an extreme mental or medical procedure using a large machine and a mental probe.
She says Aghnar's anxiety will interfere and asks to be left alone with Tonto so she can focus.
A robotic assistant reports that the instruments and deep-reaching mental probe are ready.
Honorata states that the operation will nearly exhaust her energy, requiring years of strict isolation afterward, and that interruption would kill her.
She asks Aghnar whether he accepts those conditions.
Aghnar protests that he does not want to lose his mother again and wants to live with both his wife and mother.
Honorata refuses that option and demands a choice between Oda and herself.
Aghnar chooses Oda, while insisting he loves both women.
Honorata approves the choice and says the Castakas must continue.
Aghnar adds that the Castakas will continue, but not as warriors, and says Oda agrees with him.
Honorata urges patience, but Aghnar firmly rejects any return to the Metabarons.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the operation is ambiguous: it is described as a mental probe, but the page does not fully explain its purpose.
The visual identity of Tonto is uncertain; the name may refer to the robot attendant or another off-panel assistant.
Some dialogue in the lower panels is small and could admit minor transcription ambiguity, though the overall meaning is clear.
Oda is mentioned in dialogue but is not clearly visible on this page.
visual_summary: In a bright, sterile chamber, a woman identified in dialogue as Honorata lies on a medical platform while a large glowing machine prepares to probe or operate on her mind. A robot attendant stands nearby. The lower panels cut to a tense face-to-face exchange between Honorata and Aghnar through glass or a partition, with Honorata warning him about the cost of saving her and forcing him to choose between her and Oda.
